binders: fp is a package with a real parameter u and a binary real operation fl_add satisfying the structural conditions listed below.
n is an arbitrary natural number.
w : Fin n → Real is an n-component real vector, with entries w₀,…,wₙ₋₁ when n>0.
hypotheses: For every real x and y, there exists a real δ depending on x and y such that |δ|≤u and fl_add(x,y)=(x+y)(1+δ).
With m = n ⊖ 1 = max(n-1,0), one has m·u<1.
Every component is nonnegative: 0≤w_i for every i∈Fin n.
The exact sum S=Σ_{i∈Fin n}w_i is nonzero.
conclusions: If Ŝ is the sequentially computed sum defined below, then |Ŝ-S|/|S| ≤ (m·u)/(1-m·u), where m=n⊖1.
mathematical_definitions: Set m = n ⊖ 1, using natural subtraction truncated at zero.
Set S = Σ_{i=0}^{n-1} w_i, the exact real sum of all entries.

Define the computed sum by Ŝ₀=0 for an empty vector, Ŝ₁=w₀ for a singleton vector, and Ŝ_{k+1}=fl_add(Ŝ_k,w_k) for k≥1. Thus Ŝ=Ŝ_n is a fixed left-to-right, left-associated sequential sum using exactly n-1 modeled additions when n≥1.
Define γ_m = (m·u)/(1-m·u). The hypothesis m·u<1 makes its denominator strictly positive.
Every absolute value is the ordinary scalar real absolute value; no vector norm occurs.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any modeled real addition operation with nonnegative error parameter u, exact left addition by zero, and a per-operation relative-error representation fl_add(x,y)=(x+y)(1+δ) with |δ|≤u, consider the fixed left-to-right computed sum of n nonnegative real inputs. If their exact sum is nonzero and (n⊖1)u<1, then the relative forward error of the computed sum is at most ((n⊖1)u)/(1-(n⊖1)u).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: Natural subtraction is truncated: n⊖1=0 for both n=0 and n=1.
When n=0, Fin 0 has no entries and its exact sum is 0, so the hypothesis S≠0 is impossible; the proposition is vacuous in dimension zero.
When n=1, the computed sum is exactly w₀, the validity condition is automatically 0<1, and both sides of the error bound are 0.
The result is restricted to componentwise nonnegative inputs. It does not assert this bound for mixed-sign data or cancellation-prone sums.
Because all entries are nonnegative and S≠0, S is in fact strictly positive, although the displayed denominator remains |S|.
The operation is evaluated in one fixed left-associated order. No claim is made for pairwise, tree-based, reordered, or otherwise associated summation.
The local witness δ is existential and may depend on both operands, hence on the current computed partial sum and next input at each step. No single shared δ is asserted.
Only a left-zero law fl_add(0,x)=x is encoded; no right-zero, commutativity, or associativity law for fl_add is assumed.

The model is over mathematical real numbers and postulates the relative-error equation for every real operand pair. No finite-format representability, rounding mode, overflow, underflow, subnormal, NaN, infinity, or exceptional-value behavior is encoded.
The conclusion is a scalar relative forward-error upper bound only; it does not state backward stability, componentwise perturbation bounds, sharpness, or attainment of the bound.
